name: Operational Management Workspace
purpose: Coordinate a scoped record collection, filters and authorized actions around repeated operational work, with an optional recoverable detail editor.
useWhen: Repeated record comparison, query refinement and operational action are all evidenced.
avoidWhen: A generic dashboard overview, public story, shopping gallery or single-record form is the primary task.

states.presentation: Show collection identity, active conditions and priority action.
Retain scope and mark stale results.

states.meaning: No results for the active scope.
states.presentation: Distinguish first use and zero matches; expose create or reset accordingly.
Keep active filters, selection identity and optional dirty draft.
Show selected identity and saved/dirty state.

transitions.focus: Retain filter trigger; clear or confirm selection scope.
Move to detail task heading or first meaningful field.
Retain query control and announce retry.

transitions.guard: Form reports a confirmed saved revision; failed save remains in form.
transitions.focus: Keep detail save control while refreshing affected records.
Restore selected record action or next surviving row.

visual.hierarchy: Workspace title and entity scope lead, followed by query, result count and collection; optional detail follows the selected record.
visual.alignment: Align title, search region and collection content edges; detail uses a separate aligned column only when readable.
visual.spacing: Separate query and result groups with a larger task gap than row spacing; avoid unrelated metric blocks between them.
visual.typography: Use a clear page heading, smaller collection labels and consistent record text; keep units and identifiers legible.
visual.emphasis: Prioritize operational exceptions and the current task over secondary metrics; do not start every workspace with KPI cards.
visual.surfaces: Use one collection surface and a meaningful detail boundary, avoiding nested decorative card frames.
visual.proportions: Allocate most working width to the current comparison task; detail must not compress columns into unreadable fragments.
visual.discoverability: Display the primary create/review action and selected-scope bulk actions near their collection context.
visual.states: Scope, count, freshness, dirty detail and partial failures remain distinct across the entire workspace.
visual.brand: Reuse application shell and component tokens; this composition prescribes relationships rather than a palette.

keyboard.result: Follow the task hierarchy; no competing focus traps.
keyboard.focus: Local component owns focus; workspace handles explicit detail entry/return.

keyboard.result: Apply the local dirty/draft policy before closing.
keyboard.focus: Return to the exact record or filter trigger.

accessibility.naming: Give the region a task-specific heading and each control a persistent name.
accessibility.semantics: Prefer native HTML structure; name status and recovery relationships.

checks.requirement: Every task and recovery action can be completed with keyboard input.
checks.passEvidence: Record the starting focus, complete the task and verify a visible logical destination.

responsive.condition: Collection, filters and editor compete for readable width or height.
responsive.restructure: Choose comparison-scroll versus single-record summary from the task. Keep identity, critical status/permission and frequent permitted action available at narrow widths; move details to a route or one modal surface. Do not nest independent vertical panes unless their task requires them.
preservedInformation: Active scope, query, sort and page
responsive.focusContinuity: Exactly one overlay owns interaction. Preserve focus and draft when switching layout; restore the invoker or a meaningful collection fallback.

responsive.condition: Workspace contains page, table, navigation or chips that overflow.
responsive.restructure: Assign one owner per axis/task: page owns ordinary vertical reading; comparison table owns necessary horizontal movement; navigation/chips wrap or provide reachable controls and reveal selection. Native scrollbar auto is default. Conceal locally only after equivalent discovery and keyboard/touch operation are demonstrated; repair accidental page overflow instead of clipping it.
responsive.focusContinuity: Match DOM task order to visible order; focused navigation, chips and records scroll into view without shifting unrelated regions.

density.useWhen: Mixed input methods, occasional use or unfamiliar terminology.
constraints: Keep controls independently reachable without overlapping hit areas.
Allow user text sizing and wrapping to determine minimum row or field height.

density.useWhen: Repeated scanning by experienced operators with a measured information need.
constraints: Reduce surrounding padding before reducing readable text size.
Preserve focus outline clearance, labels and distinct control targets.

motion.purpose: Explain a local state change without interrupting the current task.
motion.trigger: User initiated disclosure or result replacement.
motion.reduced: Replace content immediately; keep textual progress and completion feedback.
motion.interruption: Cancel obsolete transitions; never queue animation behind new input or block retry.

recovery.explanation: Retry collection fetch while preserving unsaved detail and active scope.

checks.requirement: Long labels, absent values and permission restrictions remain distinguishable.
checks.passEvidence: Inspect narrow and wide views with synthetic long labels and missing data.

checks.requirement: Failure preserves user intent and exposes an operable next step.
checks.passEvidence: Inject failure, retry and confirm identity, entered values and focus remain coherent.

checks.requirement: Failure when ordinary page content produces unintended horizontal overflow; a declared two-dimensional comparison region is evaluated separately.
checks.passEvidence: At 375, 768 and 1440 CSS px and enlarged text, measure document width and locate the offending node; repair its layout instead of globally clipping overflow.

checks.requirement: Review each genuinely overflowing region for a perceptible cue or reachable alternative control, plus keyboard and touch access.
checks.passEvidence: Record axis, task, accessible name, focus path and cue/control; test keyboard scrolling or equivalent navigation and swipe. Hidden scrollbar alone is neither pass nor failure.

checks.requirement: Review multiple scroll owners; unnecessary same-axis nesting can strand focus, wheel or touch input.
checks.passEvidence: Inventory page, collection, filter and dialog scroll owners; justify containment per task and exercise boundaries. Region count alone cannot determine a failure.

checks.requirement: Failure when a layout change loses the focused record/field, enters a hidden duplicate or changes keyboard task order incoherently.
checks.passEvidence: Resize with a field or row action focused; preserve identity, draft/query and logical order, then complete the task in both Tab directions.

checks.requirement: Failure when the declared essential action or state-recovery control is clipped or requires traversing unrelated horizontal columns.
checks.passEvidence: Complete the declared primary task at 375/768/1440 and 375 by 500; verify permissions, no accidental page overflow, stable focus and accessible filters in populated/empty/error/edit states.

sharedState.resetWhen: Commit filter draft; URL contains only approved shareable state.
Reset to first page when active query changes.
Filter commit clears selection or prompts for explicit scope retention.
Confirmed save invalidates the matching collection revision; preserve dirty draft during conflicts.
Detail closes; restore record focus or nearest surviving row.

actionPriority: Current record identity and collection task precede secondary metrics.
Keep the frequent collection action visible; bulk actions only apply to a labeled selected scope.
Permission checks and consequential confirmation belong to the application; unavailable actions explain why.
extensionPoints: Supply domain-specific identifiers, units and status vocabulary without changing native semantics.
Declare role permissions, data freshness, conflict policy and consequential action confirmation.
Scheduling collision detection, regulated approvals, media management and editable grids need separate specifications.
domainDefaults: Assume no healthcare, financial, education or competition policy expertise.
Use labeled generic records and application-owned permissions until explicit domain evidence is supplied.

layoutModes.condition: Wide collection and detail both remain readable.
layoutModes.restructuring: Use aligned query and results; optional detail is subordinate to the selected record.

Prioritize query/scope, then record identity/status and frequent action at horizontal origin. Choose table scrolling for comparison or summary/details for individual work; move editor to one focus-managed surface or route, preserve query/draft and avoid redundant scrollbars in empty states.
